It should be noted that at the connection between the benzene ring on the right side of the figure and the tetrahedral carbon, an intermediate aryloxy O is not clearly marked, and visually there is slight ambiguity; the standard answer interprets this connection according to the intended meaning of the problem as an aryl–O–C fragment. Reasoning: After pushing the arrows, the upper O⁻ becomes the carbonyl oxygen, and the lower OH leaves to become [OH-]; under the standard/intended interpretation, the aryl–O–C(H) skeleton remains unchanged, therefore giving p-hydroxyphenyl formate and hydroxide. The corresponding SMILES is Oc1ccc(OC([H])=O)cc1.[OH-].
